newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FOCUS-Taiwan dollar back from 9-year brink at close.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Taiwan dollar back from 9-year brink at close.

text.p: Strong intervention, apparently orchestrated by the central bank, in the final seconds of Thursday's trade pulled the Taiwan dollar back from the brink of another nine-year closing low, dealers said.
The local dollar once tumbled to as low as T$28.970 in brisk late trade before rebounding sharply as the clock ran out to close at T$28.639 against Wednesday's T$28.656 finish.
Turnover through dealers was extremely hectic at US$572 million -- some US$186 million of it in the final minutes.
The central bank declined to confirm or deny whether it had intervened to defend the Taiwan dollar.
"No central bank in the world will tell you if there is any intervention," a central bank official told reporters after the market closed.
"Go and ask the market," the official said.
The answer was yes, dealers said.
With greenback buying heavy throughout much of the session, some dealers had predicted the central bank would step in and intervene in defence of the local dollar.
"U.S. dollar buying is very heavy, but I don't think the central bank will allow such a sharp depreciation," one dealer said just before the final flurry of greenback selling.
"There is still one minute left, let's wait and see."
Sure enough, the sagging rate promptly rose -- a dramatic reverse that dealers said had all the earmarks of intervention.
Dealers said the central bank's dramatic move was a clear attempt to rein in offshore speculators, who had been buying U.S. dollars in the form of non-delivery forward trading.
"It's obvious that the central bank was punishing those offshore speculators -- who were perceived as the abnormal factors by the central bank," the dealer said.
"The central bank had repeatedly said it would intervene when abnormal factors occur. Its determination is unquestionable," the dealer said.
The bank has said a Southeast Asia-style currency trouble could not happen in Taiwan because the government can marshal appropriate defences.
Dealers said the central bank would continue to smooth, if not halt, the currency's fall amid strong greenback demand.
"I think the market has learned its lesson. It will definitely behave tomorrow," the dealer said.
Dealers saw a T$28.60-80 range for Friday.
The central bank official said its attitude towards the foreign exchange market remained unchanged.

Taiwan's central bank announced on July 31 a modest tightening of monetary policy by raising two key rates in a bid to maintain forex market stability -- though analysts said they suspected the bank also wanted to cool the stock market's hefty recent turnover.
The bank has said it would leave the Taiwan dollar exchange rate at the mercy of market forces, but with one caveat.
"The central bank will respect market forces and let market supply and demand determine the Taiwan dollar exchange rates," central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said.
"But if there are abnormal factors intervening in the market, it will adopt appropriate measures to maintain the foreign exchange market's stability," he said.
